                                         1. Introduction                                                    world tasks requiring multi-view or object-centered reason-
                                                                                                            ing, such as autonomous driving [43] and robotic manipu-
                                         Vision–language models (VLMs) have rapidly evolved,
                                                                                                            lation [36, 46].
                                         bridging visual perception and language understanding
                                                                                                                Several strategies have been explored to address the lim-
                                         through large-scale multimodal learning [1, 10, 34]. Early
                                                                                                            itations of allocentric spatial reasoning. A natural approach
                                         models excelled in perception-focused tasks such as vi-
                                                                                                            is to train models from scratch on allocentric datasets [22,
                                         sual question answering and image captioning [15, 18, 47].
                                                                                                            51], mirroring how egocentric spatial skills are typically ac-
                                         These advances have transformed VLMs from perception-
                                                                                                            quired. Although such models can reach performance lev-
                                         oriented systems into general reasoning engines capable
                                                                                                            els comparable to egocentric reasoning, the scarcity of allo-
                                         of understanding spatial structures and interacting with the
                                                                                                            centric data and the high computational cost make this ap-
                                         physical world. In particular, spatial reasoning, which in-
                                                                                                            proach impractical at scale. Fine-tuning pre-trained VLMs
                                         volves interpreting and inferring object relationships in
                                                                                                            offers a more feasible alternative [36], but these models
                                         three-dimensional (3D) space, has become essential for em-
                                                                                                            often generalize poorly beyond training contexts and suf-

   Building on these factors, we propose Symbolic                    2.2. Allocentric Spatial Reasoning
Projective Layout (SymPL), which reformulates allocentric
questions into symbolic layouts that align with the reason-          Allocentric spatial reasoning refers to the ability to under-
ing patterns VLMs inherently handle well. As illustrated in          stand spatial relationships from the viewpoints of other ob-
Figure 1, SymPL estimates 3D information from the im-                jects in the scene rather than from the observer’s perspec-
age and question, applies an orthogonal projection for rela-         tive [2, 13]. This ability is essential for real-world appli-
tional comparison (projection), abstracts objects into min-          cations that require understanding spatial relations based
imal symbols (abstraction), partitions the space into two            on surrounding objects, such as autonomous driving [43]
colored regions (bipartition), and converts the query into           and robotic interaction [36, 46]. Accordingly, several stud-
a position-estimation task (localization). These steps yield         ies have been proposed to improve this reasoning capabil-
a concise symbolic-layout question that preserves essential          ity. Some approaches address this problem by training mod-
spatial cues while filtering out redundant details, which can        els with allocentric datasets, yet they rely on costly data
also be applied to egocentric spatial reasoning. Our exper-          such as multi-view images or videos and learn only lim-
iments show that symbolic-layout questions substantially             ited positional relations [22, 36]. As an alternative, APC
improve perspective-aware spatial reasoning accuracy and             reformulates the task into an egocentric form without ad-
consistency. They preserve essential relational information          ditional training [21], leveraging auxiliary information ex-
while removing distracting cues, yielding clear gains in al-         tracted from foundation models [3, 19, 30, 41]. However,
locentric reasoning and also enhancing performance under             this conversion still falls short of leveraging the intrinsic
egocentric, visual-illusion, and multi-view conditions. The          reasoning capacity of VLMs.

4.6.2. Ablation on the Effectiveness of the Key Factor                                                           In this paper, we introduce SymPL, a framework that opti-
An ablation study was conducted to examine how the per-                                                          mizes complex spatial reasoning problem into forms where
formance on symbolic-layout questions changes as four key                                                        VLMs excel effectively. SymPL reformulates questions into
factors are added step by step. The experimental setup and                                                       intuitive symbolic-layout questions based on four key fac-
results were summarized in Table 5. Starting from Set-                                                           tors, enabling effective reasoning. Our experiments show
ting 1, we sequentially incorporate projection, abstraction,                                                     that symbolic-layout questions significantly improve both
bipartition, and localization, yielding the full symbolic-                                                       allocentric and egocentric spatial reasoning. These results
